learn.title: First in, first out
learn.body: A queue gives items back in the order they arrived: first in, first out, like people in a line. `enqueue` adds at the back and `dequeue` removes from the front.

learn.title: Wrapping around
learn.body: With an array, removing from the front would leave unused slots there. So keep `head`, the index of the front, and `count`. Use `% 4` to wrap indexes back to 0. The array acts like a circle.

learn.title: A queue of four
learn.body: `head` is the front slot. `count` is how many items are stored.

learn.title: enqueue
learn.body: The back slot is `head + count`, wrapped by `% 4`.

learn.title: dequeue
learn.body: Read the front item, move `head` forward with wrapping, and drop `count`.

learn.title: Watching it wrap
learn.body: Enqueue 1, 2, 3, dequeue once, then enqueue 4 and 5.
steps: After three enqueues, head is 0 and count is 3
Enqueue 5 goes to slot (1 + 3) % 4 = 0, wrapping around

questions.explanation: A queue is first in, first out.

questions.prompt: You enqueue 1, 2, 3 then dequeue once. What value comes out?
questions.explanation: The first item enqueued leaves first.

questions.prompt: What is the main problem a circular array solves?
choices: Wasted slots at the front after dequeues
questions.explanation: Wrapping with the modulo operator lets freed front slots be reused.

questions.prompt: A queue has capacity 4, head 3 and count 1. What slot does the next enqueue use? (3 + 1) % 4 = ?
questions.explanation: Index 4 does not exist, so it wraps to 0.

questions.prompt: A stack is last in, first out. A queue is \_\_.
questions.explanation: Queues serve items in arrival order.

questions.prompt: Match each structure to the order it returns items.
questions.explanation: Stacks reverse order. Queues keep it.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of `dequeue` in the code.
